Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) inherently produce redundant information through overlapping partitions. This characteristic, while beneficial for robustness and generalization, represents an underutilized aspect that could be leveraged for superior task performance. In this study, we introduce a novel framework known as Graph Reinforcement Learning (GRL), which constructs a new, potentially more efficient graph utilizing non-redundant parts from an initial input graph trained on specific objectives. Uniquely, GRL operates without requiring additional labeled training data; instead, it relies solely on the initial graph and objective-driven learning. Evaluations across various classification and regression tasks demonstrate that objectivity-calibrated, learning-driven graph generation can effectively enhance the efficacy of GNNs.
